practice_description.medium: Collective releasing infrastructure, legal/economic framework design, publishing platform, policy advocacy
practice_description.practice_summary: Metalabel is a collective releasing infrastructure founded by Yancey Strickler (Kickstarter co-founder) that enables groups to publish creative work together, split revenue automatically, and operate as creative units. It has evolved from a platform into a broader movement encompassing Artist Corporations (A-Corps), Dark Forest OS, and policy advocacy for new legal structures for creative people.
practice_description.methodology: Metalabel operates as a platform where creative groups create shared label pages, publish releases together, and automatically split revenue. The methodology is 'groupcore' -- groups as the primary creative unit rather than individuals. In 2025-2026, the project expanded into policy advocacy: drafting legislation for Artist Corporations (A-Corps) as a new corporate legal type in Colorado, establishing the Artist Corporations Foundation (501c3), and building Dark Forest OS (DFOS) for shared private internets. More than 4,000 artists have signed up to become an A-Corp.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Metalabel directly addresses the governance and economic infrastructure layer that A(DAI) needs for collective creative work. Its 'groupcore' philosophy aligns with A(DAI)'s commons-first approach, and the A-Corp legal structure could provide a formal framework for how collective creative intelligence is owned and governed.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: No. Metalabel is infrastructure for releasing creative work, not a system where art functions as compositional substrate. The releases (books, music, zines, NFTs) are end products rather than inputs to a generative system.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Partially. Metalabel's core mechanic is relational -- groups form around shared creative identity, and releases are collaborative products of those relationships. However, the relations are social/economic (who collaborates with whom, how revenue splits) rather than compositional (art determined by connections between elements).
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: No. Releases are fixed creative products. However, the group structures on Metalabel can evolve -- members join and leave, revenue splits change, new releases redefine the group's identity. The social composition is dynamic even if individual releases are static.

works.title: Artist Corporations (A-Corps) legislation
works.description: A proposed new corporate legal form designed specifically for creative people, with collective ownership, shares, IP management tools, and multiple revenue streams. Legislation being introduced in Colorado and other US states in 2026.
works.relevance: A-Corps could provide the legal structure for A(DAI) or similar commons-first creative intelligence projects. Demonstrates how infrastructure design extends beyond technology into law and governance.

works.title: Dark Forest OS (DFOS)
works.description: Infrastructure for shared private internets where groups can collaborate, generate revenue, and build meaning together. An extension of The Dark Forest Collective's philosophy.
works.relevance: DFOS addresses the 'commons that are not fully public' design space -- relevant to A(DAI)'s thinking about what intelligence should be open, what should be shared within communities, and what should be private.

works.title: The Dark Forest Collective releases
works.description: Strickler's own creative group that has earned $60,000 through Metalabel, demonstrating the platform's revenue-splitting model. YACHT sold out 100 vinyl copies in 90 minutes on the platform.
works.relevance: Proof that collective releasing infrastructure works economically. Demonstrates a viable alternative to individualist creator economy models.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Metalabel is one of the most explicit examples of protocol-as-creative-practice in the current landscape. The platform, the A-Corp legal structure, DFOS, and the 'groupcore' philosophy are all forms of system design intended to reshape how creative work is made, owned, and distributed. Strickler explicitly frames governance infrastructure as a creative act -- designing the rules that shape what creative communities can do.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Metalabel (collective releasing platform with automatic revenue splitting), Artist Corporations (new US corporate legal form for creative people), Artist Corporations Foundation (501c3 nonprofit), Dark Forest OS (infrastructure for shared private internets), and the broader 'groupcore' framework for collective creative identity.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Metalabel is deeply commons-oriented. The A-Corp model is explicitly designed as an alternative to C-Corps (value extraction), proposing A-Corps (creative manifestation) as a competing economic model. The Artist Corporations Foundation is a nonprofit. DFOS builds shared infrastructure for groups. The platform enables collective ownership and revenue sharing. Strickler's vision is for an 'A-Corp economy' that competes with the C-Corp economy. However, Metalabel itself is a company (not a cooperative or commons entity), and A-Corps are still a corporate form, albeit one designed for creative purposes.

governance_model.governance_detail: Metalabel is led by Yancey Strickler. The Artist Corporations Foundation has a formal board (Jennifer Arceneaux, Mikael Moore / CEO of Wondaland, with Strickler as Executive Director and Lena Imamura as Managing Director). Individual Metalabels (groups on the platform) govern themselves -- each group sets its own revenue splits and membership. A-Corps, once legislated, would have collective ownership with shares and defined governance structures. The vision is distributed governance, but current implementation is founder-led.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Groups voluntarily form Metalabels and agree on revenue splits and membership. Contributors to releases opt in. A-Corps would formalize consent through legal corporate structures with defined ownership shares and governance.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Collective authorship is the core model. Metalabel's entire premise is 'groupcore' -- groups as the primary creative unit. Releases are attributed to the group (Metalabel) rather than individuals, though individual contributions can be acknowledged. Revenue splitting makes economic authorship explicit and quantified.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Individual releases are static creative products. Groups (Metalabels) are ongoing entities that evolve over time through new releases and changing membership. The broader Metalabel ecosystem is continuously evolving as new groups form, A-Corp legislation advances, and DFOS develops.

data_materiality.data_sources: Creative releases (books, music, zines, NFTs, digital works), group membership data, revenue split configurations, policy research and legislative drafts, community survey data (Anonymous Creative Futures surveys).
data_materiality.data_provenance: Self-generated by groups and individuals on the platform. Policy research involves commissioned economic analysis and legislative drafting. Community surveys collect consented participant input.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Metalabel does not engage with embedding or latent spaces. It operates in the social, economic, and legal dimensions of creative infrastructure rather than the computational or generative dimensions.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: No. The platform hosts diverse media types (text, music, visual art) but does not unify them in a computational space.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Web-based platform. Each Metalabel has a label page displaying releases. Releases can link to external content. The platform is a publishing/commerce interface rather than an exhibition space. DFOS operates as a private web-based social space.

interoperability.composability: Moderate. Metalabel releases can link to external platforms and content. Revenue splitting is built into the platform. A-Corps, once legislated, would be interoperable with existing legal and financial infrastructure. DFOS is designed as shared infrastructure. However, the platform does not expose a public API [uncertain].
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed platform [uncertain]. The A-Corp legal framework would be open (legislation is public). DFOS model is unclear. The philosophical commitment to commons suggests eventual openness, but current technical implementation details are not publicly documented.

technical_approach.stack: Web platform (technology stack not publicly documented [uncertain]), payment processing for revenue splitting, DFOS infrastructure for private group spaces. Previously explored blockchain/NFT integration but current focus is on legal and web infrastructure.

network_position.scene_affiliation: Bridges the creative technology scene, policy/governance world, and institutional art ecosystem. Connected to Kickstarter community (Strickler's previous venture), New Museum / New Inc (release partnership), crypto-art communities (Dark Forest origins), and policy networks in Colorado and beyond. Joshua Citarella's Do Not Research initiative releases on Metalabel.
network_position.connections: Are.na (shared New Inc ecosystem, overlapping creative commons values, shared New York new media community), Rhizome / New Museum (New Inc partnership), Art Blocks (shared generative/crypto-art adjacent community)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Metalabel's A-Corp legal structure could provide the governance and ownership framework for A(DAI) as a collective intelligence commons. The 'groupcore' philosophy directly aligns with A(DAI)'s vision of collective intelligence. Metalabel's revenue-splitting model could inform how value flows through A(DAI)'s contributor network. Strickler's experience building Kickstarter and navigating platform economics is directly relevant to A(DAI)'s commons-first design challenges. DFOS could provide the private collaboration layer for A(DAI)'s team operations.
